messages:
raj: Quick sync — thinking about adding a lightweight 'pacing' layer to handle short bursts/abuse while preserving SLA for Dedicated tenants. Ideas? :thinking:
sarah: Two high-level approaches: per-tenant token buckets (refill tied to SLA tier) or a global adaptive pacing that punishes high-abuse signals. Both have tradeoffs.
emily: I lean per-tenant bucket + probation window. If tenant blasts past burst, move to probation: reduced concurrency + slow refill.
lee: Main risk is state/coordination. Per-tenant buckets at Dedicated scale means sharded state and lease logic. How do we keep it cheap?
omar: Keep a local fast-path counter per instance and a coordinator for heavier limits. Local accepts up to local_bucket, coordinator enforces global ceilings. If lease lost -> soft-shed.
sarah: Soft-shed strategies we should support: queue with ETA header, 429+Retry-After, or route to low-cost model path. Each has different UX for customers.
ops-bot: incident:rate-limiter triggered for tenant:T-42 3m ago — alerting page sent; client saw ~12s of 429s then recovered.
raj: Here's a quick mock config for mapping SLA -> refill/burst:
```yaml
tiers:
  - name: free
    refill_per_min: 500
    burst: 1000
  - name: standard
    refill_per_min: 5000
    burst: 20000
  - name: enterprise
    refill_per_min: 50000
    burst: 200000
    probation:
      concurrency: 2
      refill_factor: 0.1
```
Thoughts?
emily: :thumbsup: But probation needs cooldown and explicit whitelist for long-running background jobs. Also we should add an abuse_score threshold to trigger probation instead of pure burst count.
lee: Sharding idea: tenant_hash % N -> lease_group_id. Coordinator keeps group tokens; local nodes keep epoch counters and a small local_bucket. On lease renewal we reconcile counters.
omar: Tradeoff note: longer lease windows reduce coordinator load but increase overshoot risk on sudden spikes. Recommend adaptive lease_time = base * max(1, burst_rate/observed_rate).
sarah: We must expose metrics: per-tenant burst_usage, probation_entered, lease_miss_count, and per-route SLA labels so ops can tie pacing to routes.
deploy-bot: deploy queued: rate-pacing-v1 -> staging at 2026-03-20T15:42Z
raj: Action items: emily -> draft probation policy PR; lee -> prototype lease sharding; omar -> instrument metrics names. I'll book 30m sync tomorrow. Thanks everyone!
